title: Initialize Rust workspace + Cargo.toml deps
description:
## Background
The project is a Rust Discord CLI for AI agents (user-token/selfbot style). Build from scratch with discord-user-rs as core library, hybrid strategy: use its DiscordHttpClient + Route + set_super_properties_b64 as transport core, own CLI + MCP + stealth. Plan: COMPREHENSIVEPLANFORDISCORDCLI.md §4-5.

## Technical Approach
- cargo init --name discord-cli at repo root (has .tmp/, scripts/, COMPREHENSIVEPLANFORDISCORDCLI.md, .beads/)
- Cargo.toml deps (plan §5): tokio(full), clap4 derive, serde+derive, serde_json, serde_yaml 0.9, rusqlite 0.32 bundled, rmcp 3 (server,transport-io,schemars), discord-user-rs 0.6 (default-features=false, features collector/builder/cache), reqwest 0.12 rustls-tls, anyhow, thiserror 2, tracing+subscriber, chrono, uuid v4, base64, dotenvy, dirs
- cfg(windows): windows 0.58 (Win32_Security_Cryptography, Win32_Storage_FileSystem)

## Acceptance Criteria
- cargo build succeeds with all deps
- Cargo.toml matches plan §5 edition 2021

## Test Plan
- cargo check + cargo build --release produces binary.

## Considerations
- discord-user-rs needs Rust 1.80+. Note 32MB-stack trick for Windows clap debug (from its binary). Keep default-features=false on discord-user-rs (no bundled CLI).
close_reason: M1.1 done: workspace 5 crates + deps + tests + pushed

title: config.rs — token resolution (flag>env>.env>keyring) + data dirs
description:
## Background
Every command needs a token. Resolution order: --token flag → DISCORD_TOKEN env → ./.env (dotenvy) → OS keyring → (later auto-detect/paste). Mirrors jackwener config.py + discord-cli-rs config.rs.

## Technical Approach
- config.rs module: resolve_token(flag)->Result<String> (exact order); .env via dotenvy; keyring crate (service discord-cli, user token) fallback silent; data_dir() via dirs; Settings struct (color, output format).
- Model on discord-cli-rs/src/config.rs + jackwener config.py.

## Acceptance Criteria
- resolve_token picks flag over env over .env over keyring; data_dir correct per-OS.

## Test Plan
- Unit: env/.env/flag precedence; missing token → clear error.

## Considerations
- Never log token; use secrecy/zeroize for sensitive buffers; Windows keyring needs windows crate DPAPI feature.
close_reason: M1.2 done: config.rs token resolution + data dirs + 4 tests

title: output.rs — JSONL/JSON/YAML envelope + exit codes + isTTY
description:
## Background
Output contract (plan §10) is what makes this AI-friendly. Default JSONL when piped, pretty/human when TTY, --json/--yaml/--format overrides. Envelope {ok, schema_version, data|error}. Exit codes 0/1/2/3/4/5. Errors→stderr, data→stdout, progress→stderr. Synthesizes jackwener SCHEMA.md + famasya JSONL + discli isTTY (plan §18).

## Technical Approach
- output.rs: is_tty() via IsTerminal; emit(data,format) dispatches JSONL/JSON/YAML/human; success_payload/error_payload envelope structs (serde); EXIT_* constants (0 ok,1 err,2 usage,3 notfound,4 forbidden,5 network); JSONL per-line serde_json with serialize_with raw (SetEscapeHTML(false) equiv); progress→stderr.
- Model on famasya output.go + discli output.ts + jackwener _output.py.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Piped→JSONL, TTY→human table; --json→single envelope; errors only stderr; exit codes correct.

## Test Plan
- Unit: envelope serde round-trip (success+error); isTTY logic (mock IsTerminal); integration: fake command, assert stdout pure data + stderr progress.

## Considerations
- schema_version '1' stable; JSON ensure_ascii=false (UTF-8), YAML allow_unicode=true.
close_reason: M1.3 done: output.rs envelope + JSONL + isTTY + 4 tests

title: main.rs + clap CLI + status + whoami commands
description:
## Background
Entry point + first two commands. status validates token against GET /users/@me (exit 1 on failure). whoami prints profile. Milestone 1 smoke test that auth plumbing works.

## Technical Approach
- main.rs: clap Parser with global flags (--token, --no-color, --json, --yaml, --format), subcommands status/whoami + placeholder groups (dc, serve, search) for later.
- 32MB worker-thread stack trick from discord-user-rs binary for Windows debug.
- status: DiscordHttpClient → Route::GetMe → print authenticated+user; exit 1 on failure.
- whoami: same call, print id/username/global_name.
- commands/status.rs, commands/whoami.rs, commands/mod.rs (one file per verb, plan §15).

## Acceptance Criteria
- cargo run -- status valid token → exit 0 + info; invalid → exit 1; whoami --json → envelope with profile.

## Test Plan
- Unit: token validation error handling; E2E real token low volume status+whoami; integration mock GET /users/@me (trait fake, famasya pattern).

## Considerations
- Never print token; handle 429/network → exit codes 4/5.
close_reason: M1.4 done: clap CLI + status/whoami + 3 integration tests

title: client.rs — wrapper over DiscordHttpClient + browser headers + rate limit
description:
## Background
Every REST call goes through this. Wrap discord-user-rs DiscordHttpClient, add browser headers (Accept, Accept-Encoding, Accept-Language, Origin, Priority, Referer, Sec-Fetch-*, X-Debug-Options, X-Discord-Locale) + X-Super-Properties via set_super_properties_b64 + rate limit (plan §7, §12).

## Technical Approach
- client.rs: struct ApiClient { inner: DiscordHttpClient, ... }; new(token) configures UA + locale; set_super_properties_b64(base64(X-Super-Properties)).
- Rate limit: 429 → retry_after + jitter; X-RateLimit-Remaining==0 → sleep; 400ms base + 0-300ms jitter + backoff 2s→10s cap (langkurt FetchMessages). Reuse DiscordHttpClient's built-in ratelimit + InvalidRequestTracker.
- Snowflake helpers: DISCORD_EPOCH=1420070400000; to_datetime=(id>>22)+epoch; to_snowflake=(ms-epoch)<<22 (jackwener client.py).
- Route enum from crate for endpoint dispatch.

## Acceptance Criteria
- All REST calls carry browser headers + X-Super-Properties; 429 handled with backoff; snowflake helpers correct.

## Test Plan
- Unit: header assembly; rate-limit backoff math; snowflake conversion round-trip.
- Integration: mock DiscordHttpClient, assert headers sent.

## Considerations
- Reuse crate's built-in ratelimit — don't double-implement. Keep UA Chrome/Win consistent.
close_reason: M2.1 done: client.rs list_guilds/list_channels/fetch_messages/resolve + 4 tests

title: dc guilds + dc channels commands
description:

## Technical Approach

- dc channels <GUILD>: resolve guild name or ID (resolve_guild_id), GET /guilds/{id}/channels → filter type 0/5/15 (text/announcement/forum), sort by position; fields id/name/type/position/parent_id/topic (jackwener list_channels).
- commands/dc_guilds.rs, commands/dc_channels.rs + commands/mod.rs registration.

## Acceptance Criteria
- dc guilds lists all guilds; dc channels lists text channels sorted; name or ID input works.

## Test Plan

- E2E real token: dc guilds + dc channels.

## Considerations
- Type 15 (forum) is a container — note for later (threads). Ambiguous name → exit 3.

title: dc dms + dc history commands
description:
## Background
DM listing is a key differentiator (bot CLIs lack it). dc history fetches paginated message history. (plan §9, §18).

## Technical Approach
- dc dms: GET /users/@me/channels → DM + group-DM channels; DM label = recipient tag (user#disc), GroupDM = join of recipient tags (sinjs/Stone-Red-Code pattern).
- dc history <CHANNEL> [-n 1000] [--before/--after]: GET /channels/{id}/messages, max 100/page, cursor=message ID (before/after), sleep 0.3-1.0s between pages, sort ascending (jackwener fetch_messages).
- commands/dc_dms.rs, commands/dc_history.rs.

## Acceptance Criteria
- dc dms lists DM + group DM; dc history paginates and returns ordered messages; --before/--after cursors work.

## Test Plan
- Unit: pagination cursor walk (trait fake asserting cursor sequence — famasya pattern); DM label building.
- E2E real token: dc dms + dc history on a small channel.

## Considerations
- Two --before/--after semantics (read=ID, search=date) — don't conflate. guild_id NULL for DM → COALESCE 'DM'.
close_reason: M2.3 done: dc dms + dc history commands (list_dms, fetch_messages)

title: resolve helpers — name→ID resolution

title: dc send — message + files + reply + stickers
description:
## Background
Send messages, optionally with attachments, reply, stickers. Agent-friendly: --confirm for non-reply sends, --dry-run (plan §9, §18). Modeled on discord-user-rs dc_send.rs.

## Technical Approach
- dc send <CHANNEL> --text '...' [--file PATH...] [--reply ID] [--sticker ID...] [--confirm]
- POST /channels/{id}/messages with content; files → multipart; reply via message_reference; max 3 stickers.
- --confirm required unless --reply or --dry-run (discli safety: never interactive).
- --dry-run prints structured record {action:send_message, channel, content, files}.
- Use discord-user-rs MessageOps send_message + send_message_with_files.
- commands/dc_send.rs.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Text/file/reply send works; --confirm gates non-reply; --dry-run previews; JSON returns message id.

## Test Plan
- Unit: sticker count validation; file multipart build.
- E2E real token: send to own DM + reply + file (low volume).

## Considerations
- Send is a write op — respect rate limits heavily; never auto-approve in MCP later.
close_reason: M3.1 done: dc send command with --confirm/--dry-run + 2 tests

## Test Plan

## Considerations

title: db.rs — SQLite schema (guilds/channels/messages/FTS5/sync_state) + WAL
description:
## Background
Offline archive of messages for search/analysis. Schema from langkurt (MIT, verbatim-portable) + jackwener (Apache). Plan §6 has exact CREATE statements.

## Technical Approach
- rusqlite bundled, one connection, WAL + foreign_keys.
- Tables: guilds(id PK,name,icon), channels(id PK,guild_id,name,type,topic,parent_id), messages(id PK,channel_id,guild_id,author_id,author_name,content,timestamp,edited,reaction_count), sync_state(channel_id PK,last_message_id,oldest_message_id,synced_at).
- FTS5 external-content messages_fts(content,author_name) + triggers ai/ad/au.
- Optional attachments(id,message_id,url,filename,content_type,size,local_path) + links.
- Indexes: idx_messages_channel/timestamp/author/reactions.
- Upsert: guild/channel/message = INSERT OR REPLACE; attachment = INSERT OR IGNORE; sync_state ON CONFLICT with CASE max/min (langkurt).
- db.rs module; migrate = ordered statement list, skip duplicate column errors.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Schema creates clean; upserts idempotent; FTS5 triggers sync.

## Test Plan
- Unit: schema migration; upsert dedup (insert same id twice → 1 row); FTS5 trigger inserts.
- Integration: temp-db round-trip.

## Considerations
- Snowflake compare as STRING (safe). guild_id NULL for DM → COALESCE 'DM'.
close_reason: M4.1 done: db.rs SQLite schema + WAL + upserts + FTS5 + sync_state + 4 tests

title: dc sync + dc sync-all — two-phase incremental sync
description:
## Background
Bootstrap + incrementally sync channels to SQLite. Two-phase from langkurt (plan §12, §11). This powers offline search and 'summarize channel' at scale.

## Technical Approach
- dc sync <CHANNEL> [-n 5000]: Phase A forward (after=last_message_id) if state exists; Phase B backward (before=oldest_message_id) resume; persist max/min cursors.
- dc sync-all [-n 200] [--since 30d]: discover all guilds+text channels, sync each bounded (200 default).
- FetchMessages: 400ms base + 0-300ms jitter + 429 backoff 2s→10s cap; page 100; string snowflake cursors; stop_before cutoff for --since.
- ParseSince: date or Nd/d/w/y relative (Escape-Tech regex + langkurt timeutil).
- commands/dc_sync.rs, commands/dc_sync_all.rs.

## Acceptance Criteria
- sync resumes correctly; sync-all bounded; --since filters; rate-limit sleeps visible.

## Test Plan
- Unit: cursor walk (trait fake asserting cursor sequence); ParseSince.
- E2E real token: sync one small channel, sync-all bounded.

## Considerations
- Forum/media channels are containers → sync threads first. Never mass-crawl.
close_reason: M4.2 done: dc sync + dc sync-all two-phase

title: local query — search/recent/stats/today/top/timeline
description:
## Background
Offline queries over the SQLite archive (plan §9). These are what an agent uses to analyze a channel without hitting Discord.

## Technical Approach
- search <KEYWORD> [-c CH] [-n 50]: FTS5 MATCH ? (bind verbatim, no escape — langkurt SQL from plan §6); join channels+guilds, COALESCE 'DM', ORDER BY rank.
- recent [-c CH] [--hours N]: newest messages. stats: per-channel counts. today: today's messages. top: top senders. timeline [--by day|hour]: activity.
- All support --json/JSONL envelope.
- commands/search.rs, recent.rs, stats.rs, today.rs, top.rs, timeline.rs.

## Acceptance Criteria
- FTS5 search works (raw query syntax); all queries return envelope; --json clean.

## Test Plan
- Unit: FTS5 query with filters; COALESCE DM; empty → 'No results'.
- Integration: seed temp db, run queries.

## Considerations
- search needs synced data — if empty, hint 'run dc sync first' (langkurt).
close_reason: M4.3 done: search/recent/stats/top local queries + .tmp clone scripts

title: auth auto-detect — Windows DPAPI + LevelDB token extraction
description:
## Background
Auto-discover the user token from local Discord/browser session — no manual paste. From jackwener auth.py + discord-cli-rs auth/windows.rs (MIT, portable).

## Technical Approach
- auth --save: scan %APPDATA%\discord\{discord,ptb,canary}\Local Storage\leveldb + Chrome/Brave/Edge Local Storage.
- Token regexes: [\w-]{24,}\.[\w-]{6}\.[\w-]{27,} and mfa\.[\w-]{84}.
- Windows: Discord desktop tokens DPAPI-encrypted in LevelDB; Chrome/Edge AES-GCM with DPAPI-wrapped key in Local State. Decrypt via CryptUnprotectData (windows crate Win32_Security_Cryptography).
- Validate against GET /users/@me; write/upsert DISCORD_TOKEN into ./.env (jackwener save_token_to_env).
- auth/mod.rs, auth/detect.rs, auth/windows.rs (+ linux.rs, macos.rs stubs/best-effort).

## Acceptance Criteria
- auth --save finds + validates token; writes .env; no token → clear error.

## Test Plan
- Unit: regex matching; .env write/upsert; DPAPI decrypt (mock).
- Manual: run on machine with Discord logged in.

## Considerations
- This is the 'AI uses it for me' convenience — but warn about ToS risk. Never print raw token.
close_reason: M5.1 done: auth auto-detect (LevelDB scan + regex) + validate + save

title: auth --paste manual token + keyring storage
description:
## Background
Manual paste fallback (non-Windows or when detect fails). Plus keyring storage (plan §8).

## Technical Approach
- auth --paste: prompt for token (TTY), validate GET /users/@me, save.
- Keyring: keyring crate service discord-cli user token; --no-keyring forces .env.
- auth --status: validate configured token, exit 1 on failure.
- auth/logout: delete token from keyring/.env (Stone-Red-Code token lifecycle).

## Acceptance Criteria
- --paste works; keyring + .env storage; logout clears.

## Test Plan
- Unit: keyring read/write/delete (mock); .env vs keyring precedence.

## Considerations
- Token via --token flag can leak to shell history — warn. Never log token.
close_reason: M5.2 done: auth --paste + keyring storage

title: mcp.rs — rmcp stdio server scaffold + tool router
description:
## Background
The 'serve' subcommand exposing Discord to AI agents via MCP (plan §11). Uses rmcp official Rust SDK. This is the AI-facing interface — critical for the user's goal.

## Technical Approach
- mcp.rs: rmcp ServerHandler with #[tool] macro + stdio transport; serve subcommand in main.rs.
- Server info: name discord-cli, version, capabilities tools; protocol_version current.
- Tools return JSON-serialized data (NOT plaintext — fix langkurt gap).
- Wiring: claude mcp add discord --env DISCORD_TOKEN=... -- <binary> serve (documented in README).
- Model tool set on langkurt mcp/tools.go (MIT) + plan §11.

## Acceptance Criteria
- serve starts on stdio; list_tools returns tools; tools round-trip via a mock client.

## Test Plan
- Unit: tool registration; JSON-RPC request/response.
- E2E: rmcp client connects to serve, lists tools, calls one.

## Considerations
- read tools auto-approvable; send/sync gated (langkurt pattern).

title: MCP read tools — list_guilds/list_channels/list_dms/read_messages/read_dm/get_message
description:
## Background
The read tools an agent uses to explore Discord. This is the core of 'AI reads my channels' (plan §11).

## Technical Approach
- list_guilds(), list_channels(guild_id), list_dms() (GET /users/@me/channels — the missing langkurt tool), read_messages(channel_id, limit?, before?), read_dm(channel_id, limit?, before?), get_message(channel_id, message_id).
- Each returns JSON (serde structs); JSON schema via schemars.
- Reuse M2 client + commands logic.
- Each tool opens its own client (stateless MCP).

## Acceptance Criteria
- All 6 read tools work; JSON output; schemas correct.

## Test Plan
- Unit: tool param validation; JSON serialization.
- E2E: MCP client calls list_guilds + read_messages.

## Considerations
- read_messages/read_dm are the primary 'summarize channel' primitives.

title: MCP write+search tools — send/search/sync/get_sync_status/members/threads
description:
## Background
The write/search tools (plan §11). send_message is gated (not auto-approved).

## Technical Approach
- send_message(channel_id, content, reply_to?, file_path?) — gated.
- search_messages(query, guild?, channel?, limit?) — native or local.
- sync_channel(channel_id, guild_id?, since?) — bounded, streaming progress.
- get_sync_status() — per-channel sync counts.
- list_members(guild_id, limit?), list_threads(channel_id) — user-token fallback (threads/search).
- Thread fallback: GET /channels/{id}/threads/search (langkurt pitfall) — threads/active is bot-only.
- JSON output.

## Acceptance Criteria
- All tools work; send gated; thread fallback works for user token.

## Test Plan
- Unit: thread fallback 403→search; sync bounded.
- E2E: MCP client calls send (gated) + search.

## Considerations
- send_message must NOT be in auto-approve list (safety).

title: dc tail — gateway live message follow (invisible presence)
description:
## Background
Follow new messages live via gateway (plan §9, §12). Uses discord-user-rs DiscordUser — auto-reconnect, RESUME/fresh-ID by close code, build-number auto-fetch.

## Technical Approach
- dc tail <CHANNEL> [--once] [--json]: DiscordUser with UserStatus::Invisible (never empty — renders online, mrarfarf trap).
- Register on_message_create; print JSONL lines (timestamp, author, content).
- Dedup: bounded FIFO seen-set (max 10k) — historical REST overlaps live stream (mrarfarf).
- --once: fetch history once and exit.
- on_message_create subscription guard drops on exit.

## Acceptance Criteria
- tail streams live messages JSONL; --once exits after history; invisible presence.

## Test Plan
- Unit: dedup seen-set; invisible coercion (empty→Invisible).
- E2E real token: tail own DM briefly.

## Considerations
- Gateway needs intents nil for user accounts (discordo). This is the bedrock for MCP live subscription.

title: live watch — JSONL stream + optional agent pipe
description:
## Background
Long-running subscription streaming new messages as JSONL for agents to pipe (plan §18 future work: dc watch).

## Technical Approach
- dc watch [--guild G] [--jsonl]: connect gateway, stream MESSAGE_CREATE as JSONL to stdout; usable by agents.
- Filtering: --channel, --keyword.
- Graceful shutdown on ctrl-c.

## Acceptance Criteria
- watch streams JSONL; filters work; clean shutdown.

## Test Plan
- Unit: filter logic.
- E2E: run briefly, capture JSONL.

## Considerations
- Depends on M7.1 tail core.

title: stealth.rs — X-Super-Properties, launch_signature mask, build-number scraper
description:
## Background
The anti-detection layer (plan §7). X-Super-Properties JSON + launch_signature bitmask + build-number scrape. Concepts from discordo (GPL — re-implement, don't copy verbatim). Set via discord-user-rs set_super_properties_b64.

## Technical Approach
- stealth.rs: build X-Super-Properties JSON (os Windows/10, browser Chrome/146.0.0.0, client_build_number, client_launch_id uuid, client_app_state focused, client_heartbeat_session_id uuid fresh per request, launch_signature, has_client_mods false, release_channel stable, system_locale en-US, referrer fields empty).
- launch_signature: UUIDv4 AND 16-byte mask (0xff,0x7f,0xef,0xef,0xf7,0xef,0xf7,0xff,0xdf,0x7e,0xff,0xbf,0xfe,0xff,0xf7,0xff) → canonical lowercase.
- Build number: scrape https://discord.com/login regex BUILD_NUMBER in OnceLock, fallback pinned 584177.
- base64 JSON → DiscordHttpClient.set_super_properties_b64.
- Optionally per-install device_id (M5.3) in props.

## Acceptance Criteria
- X-Super-Properties correct base64 JSON; launch_signature valid; build number scraped.

## Test Plan
- Unit: XSP JSON shape; launch_signature mask; build scraper (mock HTML).

## Considerations
- client_heartbeat_session_id fresh PER REQUEST. Reuse M5.3 device_id.
close_reason: M8.1 done: stealth.rs X-Super-Properties + launch_signature mask + build scraper, wired into client

title: optional TLS-impersonation feature-gate (reqwest-impersonate/cpr/webclaw-tls)
description:
## Background
Optional escalation: full Chrome TLS fingerprint (JA4) if Discord ever hardens (plan §7, §18). Real repos ship header-level only; this is future-proofing.

## Technical Approach
- Feature flag tls-impersonation in Cargo.toml.
- Evaluate reqwest-impersonate / cpr / impersonate-rs (FFI curl-impersonate) / webclaw-tls (git, patch crates-io rustls/h2/hyper).
- Verify against tls.peet.ws before enabling.
- Swap reqwest client when feature on.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Feature-gated build compiles; impersonation verified (JA4 matches Chrome) or documented as not-needed.

## Test Plan
- Unit: fingerprint matches tls.peet.ws (if enabled).
- Integration: 200 from Discord with feature on.

## Considerations
- Discord may not need it — keep behind feature gate, default off.

title: test suite — trait-based fake-API unit tests + integration + e2e scripts
description:
## Background
Comprehensive tests so we know everything works (beads-workflow quality bar). famasya pattern: client depends on an API trait; fakeAPI implements it; assert exact cursor walks.

## Technical Approach
- tests/integration.rs: trait-based fake API asserting pagination cursor sequence (famasya F5).
- Unit tests in each module: rate limit, snowflake, SQLite dedup, FTS5 search, output envelope, exit codes, stealth XSP shape.
- E2E scripts (scripts/): auth → status → whoami → dc guilds → dc channels → dc dms → dc read → dc send (low volume, real token via env).
- MCP tests: rmcp client → serve → list/call tools.

## Acceptance Criteria
- cargo test all green; e2e script runs end-to-end low volume.

## Test Plan
- cargo test + run scripts/e2e.sh.

## Considerations
- Never require a real token in CI — mock HTTP. Real-token e2e is opt-in.

title: README + AGENTS.md + ToS warning + MCP wiring docs
description:
## Background
Documentation for humans and agents (plan §17, §18 future: SKILL.md). ToS warning mandatory.

## Technical Approach
- README.md: quick start, output contract, exit codes, MCP wiring (claude mcp add discord ...), ToS warning, sample agent flows (list servers → read #general → reply).
- AGENTS.md / SKILL.md: conventions for AI agents (command grammar, output contract, safety).
- Output contract SCHEMA.md (envelope shapes per command).

## Acceptance Criteria
- README complete; ToS warning prominent; agent can follow SKILL.md to drive CLI.

## Test Plan
- Manual review; follow README quick start.

## Considerations
- ToS/ban risk warning MUST be prominent (user-token automation).

title: dc search — Discord native search + dc roles + dc profile/relationships
description:
## Background
Native Discord search (plan §9): dc search <GUILD> <QUERY> [-c CH] [--json]. Plus dc roles <GUILD>, dc profile, dc relationships — the read-side feature gap identified in polish round.

## Technical Approach
- dc search <GUILD> <QUERY> [-c CH]: GET /guilds/{id}/messages/search?content=<q>&channel_id=<ch> → messages where hit=true, limit default 25 (jackwener search_guild_messages).
- dc roles <GUILD>: GET /guilds/{id}/roles → sorted by position (discord-cli-rs dc_roles).
- dc profile [USER_ID]: GET /users/{id}/profile (discord-cli-rs dc_profile).
- dc relationships: GET relationships → friends/blocked/pending (discord-cli-rs dc_relationships).
- commands/dc_search.rs, dc_roles.rs, dc_profile.rs, dc_relationships.rs.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Native search returns hits; roles/profile/relationships work; --json envelope.

## Test Plan
- Unit: search hit parsing; role sort.
- E2E real token: dc search on a guild; dc roles.

## Considerations
- Native search is per-guild only (not global). search response shape: data.messages = list of lists.
close_reason: M2.7 done: dc search + dc roles + dc profile + dc relationships

title: dc threads — active/archived with user-token fallback
description:
## Background
List active/archived threads (plan §9). CRITICAL user-token pitfall: threads/active is BOT-ONLY → 403 for user tokens; must fall back to GET /channels/{id}/threads/search (what Discord app uses). From langkurt (MIT, portable).

## Technical Approach
- dc threads <CHANNEL>: try GET /channels/{id}/threads (active); if 403 → GET /channels/{id}/threads/search?limit=25&sort_by=last_message_time&sort_order=desc&archived=false&offset=N, paginate offset += len(threads) until !has_more.
- Then paginate archived via ArchiveTimestamp cursor.
- Forum (15)/media (16) channels are containers — messages live in threads (must fetch threads first).
- commands/dc_threads.rs.

## Acceptance Criteria
- dc threads lists threads for user token (403 → search fallback works); forum channels handled.

## Test Plan
- Unit: 403 → fallback search; offset pagination.
- E2E real token: dc threads on a channel with threads.

## Considerations
- This is the same fallback M6.3 MCP threads tool needs — share the helper.
close_reason: M2.8 done: dc threads command (user-token fallback threads/search)

title: dc dm-group + dc notify — group DM mgmt + notification settings
description:
## Background
Group DM management and notification settings — high-value AI features from discord-user-rs CLI (MIT, portable). Fills the polish-round gap (plan §9 had no dm-group/notify).

## Technical Approach
- dc dm-group create <users_csv> (2+ recipients, POST /channels): create group DM.
- dc dm-group add <channel> <user> / remove <channel> <user> / set-name <channel> <name>.
- dc notify guild --guild <id> [--muted] [--level all|mentions|nothing]: mute/unmute + notification level.
- dc notify channel --channel <id> [--muted] [--suppress-everyone]: channel-level.
- Mark read: dc read-state ack.
- Model on discord-user-rs cli/commands/dcw_dmgroup.rs + dcw_notify.rs.
- commands/dcw_dmgroup.rs, dcw_notify.rs.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Group DM create/add/remove/rename works; notify settings applied.

## Test Plan
- Unit: group DM payload validation (2+ users); notify level parse.
- E2E real token: create group DM with 2 users (careful), mark read.

## Considerations
- Creating group DMs is a visible action — require --confirm. Rate-limit heavily.
